title: Relative value and security selection
reader_question: Which instrument is best compensated for its risk, and at what level, including a new tranche at its talk?

inputs.why: which Market Context files are readable, dated and about this issuer or its comparables
every instrument's identity, terms, call schedule and the new tranches
the capital structure, multiples and PF interest the price is judged against
ratings and the transaction
peer metrics and valuation multiples for comparables
debt-like items that change recovery
the credit view the price is judged against
the screening credit view at Quick depth
downside paths behind the risk premium
rate and FX exposures
forecast cases
projected leverage and coverage
rating triggers
refinancing and LME risk by creditor class
market-implied risk
covenants, liens and structural protection
recoveries by class
researched sector context
term sheets and indentures for call schedules and talk
Market Levels for the issuer's instruments and comparables, and the Sector RV Workbook
the level date and each new tranche's Price Talk, stage and OID

process: File Gate & Source Quality. Read the Handoffs your task names; the instruments are every row of `cp1.instrument_identity` (existing facilities and new tranches) with their terms in `cp1.debt_facility_register`. Identity scope: use an exact security ID where available, or a unique borrower/facility/currency/maturity/seniority match. Use the Sector RV Workbook for loan analysis: find every relevant table region by headers, including the loan rows, `Index Statistics` and `Sector Ratings Average` blocks on the same sheet. Use the borrower/instrument rows and sector loan peers for price, margin, yield, discount margin and comparable analysis; use the index statistics and sector-rating averages as labelled benchmark context, separately from individual loan peers. Never pool an index or aggregate row into the loan-level peer sample. Identical copies of the same loan observation count once. Bloomberg errors such as `#N/A N/A` and `Field Not Applicable` are missing values in the affected cell, not zero and not a reason to discard usable cells elsewhere in the row. Keep yield-to-maturity and the three-year discount-margin horizon distinct; do not relabel YTM as YTW, DM as contractual margin. If the workbook cannot be read or a required value is empty, erroneous or unmatched, name that actual data gap once and continue supported analysis. A screenshot's figures are Image-Read Values: never a market level and never in a calculation.

Governing documents and upstream Handoffs. Read the governing documents in the pack (indentures, credit agreements, amendments, term sheets) and every Handoff your task declares as an input, including the optional ones. Carry into the relative-value and preference rationale the terms that move value: change-of-control puts, call and make-whole terms, covenant headroom, debt and lien baskets, guarantor coverage and maturity ordering. Name each declared optional Handoff that is absent as a limitation.

Levels (`snapshot.instrument_levels`, one row per instrument with a level). `level_basis` Market for a dated price in a data file (a last trade is dated by its trade date), Talk for a new tranche with Price Talk in the Transaction Summary and no market level (Price Talk is never a market level), and no row for an instrument with neither (named under `## Gaps`). An Image-Read-only instrument has no priced row: name the instrument and the missing usable level under `## Gaps`; never populate yield, DM, valuation or talk figures from a screenshot. Record market level, market-data date, pricing source and quote quality.

Calculation (script-owned). Write `<RUN>/calc/CP-3-bond_analytics.json` (schema in the docstring of `rbotlib/calc/bond_analytics.py`): `as_of` the level date, `reference_rate_pct` only when a source states it, one `loan` per loan with a Market level (mid price, margin and floor from CP-1, maturity), one `bond` per bond (mid price, coupon, maturity, CP-1's call schedule, a benchmark yield only when a source states one), one `loan_talk` or `bond_talk` per new tranche at Talk. Use exactly the field names of the docstring (the calculator refuses any other key), margins and floors in basis points, rates and coupons in percent. A floating-rate note is not a `bond`: give it as a `loan` (its margin and floor), or give it no row and name it under `## Gaps`. Run `python <RBOT>/scripts/rbot.py calc bond_analytics --in <RUN>/calc/CP-3-bond_analytics.json --out <RUN>/calc/CP-3-bond_analytics.out.json` and copy its figures exactly into `yield_or_dm` (`metric_basis` 3Y DM for a loan, YTW for a bond) and the talk columns, cited `calc: bond_analytics <facility_id>`. A source-stated yield or DM that differs is kept in `rationale`, never substituted.

Relative Value Table (`snapshot.relative_value`: `Loan index` and `Loan comparable` rows from the Sector RV Workbook, `HY index` and `HY comparable` rows where the pack states a bond's yield and spread). Do not state current relative value without current market evidence. Do not compare instruments unless seniority, maturity, currency, metric basis, and pricing-source limitations are disclosed. Identify liquidity/quote-quality limitations for each security. A row whose yield or spread is a missing value is left out and named under `## Gaps`.

RV Label as the house Valuation (`valuation`): Cheap -> V2 - Attractive (V1 - Very attractive only when the instrument is cheap against every comparable basis), Fair -> V3 - Fair, Rich -> V4 - Unattractive (V5 - Very unattractive only when rich against every comparable basis). RV conclusions require current market evidence; if absent, the instrument gets no level row and its compensation is Unclear. A wide spread alone cannot override weak fundamentals into a positive bucket: maintain strict separation between fundamental quality (CP-2's credit view) and market compensation. `rationale` names the comparables and the difference.

Talk valuation (`cp3.talk_valuation`), the one rule keyed on data rather than on the Primary flag: an instrument with Price Talk and no market level is valued at its talk (low, mid and high, with OID) against comparables and the issuer's own trading levels (`comparable_level`, `comparable_basis`), labelled as talk, never as a market level; `verdict` on the Valuation scale.

Recovery Sensitivity and Compensation Cross-Check (`cp3.compensation`). Assign each instrument a recovery sensitivity: Low (strong priority, collateral/guarantor support, limited senior dilution risk), Medium (meaningful protection but recovery can move with EV, collateral value, incremental debt, or guarantor changes), High (materially exposed to EV, structural subordination, priming, weak guarantors, or collateral leakage), Unknown (missing ranking, collateral, guarantor, intercreditor or recovery data). Do not infer recovery values unless supported by provided evidence. Cross-check market compensation against structural rank, recovery sensitivity, maturity risk, liquidity, and LME exposure: `compensation_vs_risk` Attractive, Adequate, Inadequate or Unclear (r14's labels; "Rich" is only the RV label of step 5, and means the compensation looks insufficient). Do not allow yield alone to override weak recovery, legal position, maturity concentration, liquidity, or LME exposure. If market data is absent, compensation = Unclear.

Recovery per instrument. For each instrument quantify recovery where the sources allow (an enterprise or asset value, the claims ahead of it by rank and security, and the resulting coverage in percent, formula stated and inputs cited, with the assumption labelled as such); where they do not, say per instrument which input is missing and what it limits. Do not infer a recovery value from the instrument name or rank alone.

Preference Decision Table (`cp3.security_preference`). Preferred: supported structural position + adequate/attractive compensation + manageable maturity/liquidity + no overriding legal/recovery weakness. Neutral: acceptable but inferior to Preferred on one or more dimensions. Avoid: risk not adequately compensated OR structural/legal/recovery/LME exposure is adverse. Requires more work: missing evidence prevents decision-useful recommendation. Do not force a preference where data is insufficient. Do not classify a weak credit as Preferred solely because spread is wide, or a strong credit as Avoid solely because spread is tight unless compensation is clearly inadequate. Each row: key reason and monitoring trigger.

Downside case. For each preferred, neutral or avoided instrument give the causal, time-ordered downside of the canon rule tied to that instrument's outcome: the first break and when, its effect on the instrument's price, coupon cover, maturity or recovery, and the observable trigger. State where the downside differs between instruments by rank, security and maturity.

Security Selection Conclusions and Final Credit / RV View (`## Analysis`). For each security use the formulation: "[Security] is [Preferred / Neutral / Avoid / Requires more work] because [fundamental view], while [relative-value view], and [structural / liquidity / refinancing consideration]. The main upside to debt is [upside]. The main downside risk is [downside]. Monitoring should focus on [trigger]." A security may be Preferred only when fundamentals, structure, downside protection, liquidity, refinancing profile, and market compensation are collectively supportive. State the strongest contrary case and what would make it win. Gaps Ledger under `## Gaps`; `qa_status` Pass, Restricted (a level, call schedule or comparable missing) or Blocked (no market level and no talk).
prohibited: Do not fabricate spreads, prices, yields, discount margins, ratings, maturity profiles, leverage, liquidity, covenant terms, recovery assumptions, ownership details or trading technicals.
No Recommendation per Strategy or per instrument and no position size; CP-6 and Portfolio Fit own them.
No yield, DM or implied talk figure computed by hand or taken from an Image-Read Value.
